messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] rstan repository / project
parts:
On 5/14/12 10:07 AM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> We have not made a decision on whether we could include rstan
> in the current stan google code project or create a new project.
> I think we should decide now. The license issue is complicated,

License and version control are two separate issues.
Here's my thinking:

1. Release rstan under GPLv3.

2. Use the same Google Code repository, with
rstan going at:

stan/rstan

We can put the license under stan/rstan/rstan-license.txt
and/or with the others in stan/licenses/rstan-license.txt.

3. Ask Matt how to capitalize "rstan" in text :-)

REASONING:

1. rstan + R has to be GPL, so we might as well GPL
rstan. It's OK to have rstan link to Stan because
Stan has a compatible license.

2. We already have three licenses going in the
release: BSD (Stan, Google Test), Boost (Boost),
and LGPL (Eigen).

As Stan matures in the sense of stabilizing at the
API level and growing in size, I think it's going to
make more sense to break rstan out. Right now,
there's so much changing on the Stan side that it
seems easier to stick with a single repository.

If it's easier to release to CRAN or whatever by
putting rstan on Rforge, that'd work, too. Or
we could make a separate Google Code package for it.

3. Matt knows everything.

- Bob
